The mechanism of botulinum toxin is thought to be due to cleavage of proteins responsible for release of neurotransmitter from the nerve endings. The target protein for botulinum toxin type A is SNAP-25.

key_safety.text: In cervical dystonia placebo-controlled trials, the most commonly reported adverse reactions (>5%) were muscular weakness, dysphagia, dry mouth, injection site discomfort, fatigue, headache, neck pain, musculoskeletal pain, dysphonia, injection site pain, and eye disorders. In the double-blind phase (DYSPORT 500 Units N=173 vs placebo N=182), muscular weakness occurred in 16% vs 4%, dysphagia 15% vs 4%, and injection site discomfort 13% vs 8%. In glabellar lines trials the most frequent events (>=2%) were nasopharyngitis, headache, injection site pain, injection site reaction, upper respiratory tract infection, eyelid edema, eyelid ptosis, sinusitis and nausea.

detail.text: Distant Spread of Toxin Effect: the effects of DYSPORT and all botulinum toxin products may spread from the area of injection to produce symptoms consistent with botulinum toxin effects; swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening and there have been reports of death. Risk is probably greatest in children treated for spasticity.

citations.quote: The effects of DYSPORT™ and all botulinum toxin products may spread from the area of injection to produce symptoms consistent with botulinum toxin effects. These symptoms have been reported hours to weeks after injection. Swallowing and breathing difficulties can be life threatening and there have been reports of death.

detail.text: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments, to ensure the benefits outweigh the risk of distant spread of botulinum toxin and the potential for medication errors related to lack of interchangeability with other botulinum toxin products.

citations.quote: In accordance with 505-1 of the FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Dysport (abobotulinumtoxinA) to ensure that the benefits of the drug outweigh the risk of distant spread of botulinum toxin after local injection, and the potential for medication errors related to the lack of interchangeability of Dysport (abobotulinumtoxinA) with other licensed botulinum toxin products.
The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

vote.text: This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because Dysport is not first in its class; its active ingredient is the same as that of Botox, and the pharmacological properties of botulinum toxin Type A are well-established.
